description: Granular texture synthesiser: it records incoming audio into a short buffer and plays it back in fragments, with six processing modes that include a reverb and a resonator

params.text: Picks the processing mode: granular, pitch shifter and time stretcher, looping delay, spectral processor, the Oliverb reverb, or the Resonestor resonator; the matrix display names it
Stops recording into the buffer so the module works on what it already holds; the small display names what it does in the mode in use, which is freeze, stutter, or a change of voice
Sets the first parameter of the mode in use — grain position, scrub, delay time, buffer choice, pre-delay or timbre — and the display under the slider names it
Sets the second parameter of the mode in use — grain density, diffusion, frame merging, reverb decay or resonator decay — and the display under the slider names it
Sets the third parameter of the mode in use — grain size, window overlap, the frequency-mapping polynomial, room size or chord — and the display under the slider names it
Sets the fourth parameter of the mode in use — grain shape, a low-pass and high-pass filter, the spectral quantiser or the reverb dampening — and the display under the slider names it
Transposes the grains, two octaves either way; in the reverb and resonator modes it sets the pitch of what they produce
Sets the level of the audio going into the buffer
Sets the balance between the dry signal and the processed one; with the Resonestor mode it sets distortion instead
Sets how far the processed signal is panned at random across the stereo field; with the reverb mode it sets diffusion and with the resonator the stereo mix
Sets how much of the processed signal is fed back into the buffer; with the reverb mode it sets modulation speed and with the resonator the string harmonics
Sets how much reverb is added to the processed signal; with the reverb mode it sets modulation depth and with the resonator the scatter
Switches the buffer between 16-bit and 8-bit recording; 8-bit doubles the buffer length and adds a companded distortion closer to tape than to hiss
Switches the buffer between stereo and mono recording; mono doubles the buffer length
Cycles what the lamp row shows: the input level, the output level, or the settings of the BLEND, SPREAD, FEEDBACK and REVERB knobs
Plays the buffer backwards in the modes that read it that way
Sets the level of the audio leaving the module; past the middle it amplifies rather than attenuates

inputs.text: A voltage of 1V or more freezes the buffer for as long as it stays high, doing what the FREEZE button does
Adds to the first slider, 5V covering the whole slider range
Adds to the second slider, 5V covering the whole slider range
Adds to the third slider, 5V covering the whole slider range
Adds to the fourth slider, 5V covering the whole slider range
Transposes the grains, one volt per octave, added to the pitch knob and limited to four octaves either way
A voltage of 1V or more acts on the mode in use: it sows a single grain, starts a stutter, sets the delay time, glitches the spectrum, clocks the reverb, or fires a burst
Adds to the BLEND knob, 5V covering the whole knob range
Adds to the SPREAD knob, 5V covering the whole knob range
Adds to the FEEDBACK knob, 5V covering the whole knob range
Adds to the REVERB knob, 5V covering the whole knob range
The left audio input; a polyphonic cable here is summed down to one channel
The right audio input; with nothing patched it reads the left input, so a single cable feeds both sides
A voltage of 1V or more plays the buffer backwards for as long as it stays high, doing what the REVERSE button does

notes: the module works in one channel per side: a polyphonic cable at either audio input is summed to a single channel, and each output carries one channel.
the buffer is short, and its length follows the two quality buttons: 1 second in 16-bit stereo, 2 seconds in 16-bit mono, 4 in 8-bit stereo and 8 in 8-bit mono.
the buffer cannot be saved or loaded here, though the hardware can do it.
bypassing the module passes the left and right inputs straight to the matching outputs.
menu: Mode: GRANULAR, STRETCH, LOOPING DLY, SPECTRAL, OLIVERB, RESONESTOR — picks the processing mode, each entry giving the display name and then the mode's full name
